name: Xanxicar

facts.text: Level 80, 100,000 health. At 80, 60, 40 and 20% he announces and brings down Xanxicar's Stomp on everything around him; from 50% Xanxicarian Champions (level 65) come one after another, 15-25 s apart, while he fights.
He hurls a random real player within 2,500 into the air every 20-40 s and glares at another; when he dies 'a glowing light begins to form on the mound'.
Two-headed, white or silver, in an archived newsgroup thread; 'well over a hundred players' (Feb 2003); five full groups wiped (Jul 2005).
Existing bot chat says the cave fills with lightning if you dawdle; nothing in the script does that. It is kept as hearsay.

story:
Xanxicar is the dragon under Avalon, and the dragon the drakoran follow. He has two heads and a hide like frost on silver, and he sleeps on a mound of crystal at the bottom of the cave, where every light is thrown back a hundred times. Whether the scholars of Avalon built their colleges over him to keep him asleep, or whether he let them, no one alive can say. When he wakes he does not breathe fire like the dragons of the realms. He uses his weight. He rears up with both heads high and brings the whole of himself down on everything near him, and he does it again each time another fifth of his strength is gone. From half his strength his champions come to him, Xanxicarian warriors who are to the drakoran what a king's household knights are to a king, one after another until he dies. He flings men into the air for the pleasure of watching them fall. When he dies a light forms on his mound.

The sleeper. Xanxicar is older than Avalon. The oldest map of the isle, drawn before the first college, already marks him at its heart. He slept under the isle while the readers built their city on top of him, while Merlin learned his letters overhead, while Morgana learned hers. The crystal of the cave grew around him over the ages, or out of him; even the Camelot loremasters cannot agree.

The waking. On the third night of the burning the readers saw a light rise from the city's heart, and many think that was Xanxicar waking. The drakoran, who had come to the isles at Morgana's call, went down to him and came up his. The Avalon Isle tales say the dragon-men are led by a huge dragon. He is that dragon, whatever the five lords say, and Dura'ek, who went down first, carries his fire and frost.

How he fights. He does not breathe like the dragons of the realms. He has two heads, and a hide like frost on silver, and he uses his weight: he rears up with both heads high and brings the whole of himself down on everything near him, and he does it again each time another fifth of his strength is gone. From half his strength his champions come to him, Xanxicarian warriors who are to the drakoran what a king's household knights are to a king, one after another until he dies. He seizes men and flings them into the air for the pleasure of watching them fall, and glares at others. When he dies a light forms on his mound, and nobody knows what it is.
legend:
Over a hundred, the old guides said; five groups wiped in one go, said another. He stomps at 80, 60, 40 and 20 percent: everyone but the tanking party gets out of range on the warning. From half, champions keep coming; one party kills each away from the tank. Some swear the cave fills with lightning if you take too long.

The guards on the way in are worse than he is; send a scout, clear the patrols, and arrive with full mana. The old hands say he is the one dragon in Albion who respects a raid that keeps its distance, and kills one that does not.

loremasterTopic.text: A dragon with two heads and a hide like frost on silver. When he wakes he rears and crushes all around him, again and again as he weakens. From half his strength his champions come to him, one after another. Keep away from his feet.

bookPage: He sleeps on a mound of stone that gives back light. When he wakes he rears up, both heads high, and brings his weight down on everything near him; the ground lurches, and those beneath him do not rise. He does this not once but as often as he is hurt, at every fifth part of his strength. At the half his champions begin to come, and they do not stop. When he dies, a light forms on the mound. A priest of Camelot who saw it wrote to me that it looked like the light we saw rise on the third night of the burning. No one has yet dared to touch it.
